title: C482/885/2011 of M/S UTTAR DEVELOPMENT PVT LTD AND ORS Vs KRIPAL SINGH

paras.text:
Reserved on 04.01.2019
Delivered on 08 .01.2019
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application No. 885 of 2011
M/s Uttar Development Pvt. Ltd. and Ors.
 Ö.. Applicants
Versus
Shri Kripal Singh Ö.Respondent
Mr. Prateek Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicants.
Mr. S.K. Chaudhary, learned counsel for the respondent.
Honíble R.C. Khulbe, J.
 By way of the present application preferred
under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 (hereinafter to be referred as ëCr.P.Cí), the
petitioners have challenged the summoning order
dated 20.06.2009 passed by the Additional Chief
Judicial Magistrate in criminal complaint case no.
1141 of 2010, Kripal Singh vs. M/s Uttar Development
Pvt. Ltd. and others, relating to offence punishable
under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act,
1881, pending in the court of Civil Judge (Sr. Div.),
Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar.
2. The facts, to the limited extent necessary,
are that the complainant-Kripal Singh filed a complaint
case against the petitioners under Section 138 of
Negotiable Instruments Act, stating therein that the
complainant was the owner of land bearing Khasra
No.1162 measuring 0.405 hectare situated at Village-Mahuwakheraganj, Tehsil-Kashipur, District Udham
Singh Nagar. The said land was sold out to the
applicant-Uttar Development Pvt. Ltd. by way of sale

2
deed dated 24.09.2008 with the consideration of
Rs.25,15,000/-. Before an agreement was executed
between the complainant and the applicants on
27.01.2007, the applicant-Uttar Development Pvt. Ltd
paid an amount of Rs.18,15,000/- against the said
consideration amount by way of cash; and a cheque
dated 15.12.2008 was issued in favour of the
complainant, which was deposited in the Oriental Bank
of Commerce, Branch, Kashipur on 26.05.2009. On the
very same date, the cheque was dishonored on account
of insufficient funds. Thereafter, the complainant
issued a notice to the applicants. In spite of due
service, the applicants have failed to pay the said
amount of cheque. Thereafter, the complaint was filed
under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
3. The complainant appeared before the
learned trial court and submitted documents in
support of his claim.
4. After hearing the complainant, the learned
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate summoned all the
applicants under Section 138 of Negotiable
Instruments Act, on 20.06.2009.
5. Aggrieved by it, this petition was filed by all
the applicants under Section 482 of Cr. P.C. for setting
aside the impugned summoning order and quashing
the proceedings.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for both the
parties and perused the record produced before this
Court.
7. This is an admitted fact that the respondent-complainant-Kripal Singh sold out his land to the

3
applicants on 24.09.2008 by way of sale deed and
Rs.18,15,000/- was paid by the applicants to the
complainant. It is also admitted that the cheque of
Rs.7.00 lakh was also issued in favour of the
complainant, which was dishonoured due to
insufficient funds in the account of applicants.
8. It is also an admitted fact that after filing of
this petition, when the case was listed on 23.09.2011,
a demand draft No. 001749 for an amount of Rs. 7
lakhs was prepared in the name of respondent-Kripal
Singh and it was further stated by the petitioners that
they are ready to pay further an amount of Rs.84,000/-
towards interest through demand draft no. 001748 to
the respondent. While, the draft was accepted it was
stated that the settlement had arrived between the
parties of Rs. 12 lakhs. Whether the said amount has
taken place or not, is not clear.
9. From the evidence produced before the
learned trial court, it is clear that the respondent sold
out his property in favour of the applicants on a
consideration of Rs.25,15,000/- out of which
Rs.18,15,000/- were paid in cash and a cheque of Rs.7
lakhs dated 15.12.2008 was issued in favour of the
respondent, but it was dishonored due to insufficient
fund. The above facts were admitted by the applicants
in this petition. Although during the course of this
petition, the applicants prepared two demand drafts for
an amount of Rs.7 lakhs and another of Rs.84,000/-
towards the interest which were given to respondent ñ
Kripal Singh. It is also admitted fact that the
respondent issued a notice to the applicants but in

4
spite of service, the applicants did not pay the said
amount to the respondent as mentioned in the cheque.
10. From the perusal of the impugned order and
record, I do not find any illegality in the impugned
summoning order. The Additional Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Kashipur after scrutinizing the evidence
has summoned the applicants under Section 138 of
Negotiable Instruments Act. In these circumstances the
present petition filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is
liable to be dismissed. The present application filed
under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is dismissed, accordingly.
The summoning order dated 20.06.2009 passed by the
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate in criminal
complaint case no. 1141 of 2010, Kripal Singh vs. M/s
Uttar Development Pvt. Ltd is hereby affirmed.
11. Since the matter relates to the year 2010,
hence the Court below is directed to decide the matter
as per the law within a period of six months from the
date of receiving the order.
12. The Registry is directed to send a copy of
this order to the Court concerned for compliance.
